title: How to Care for Your Wool Clothes This Winter
excerpt: Wool is a delicate fabric that needs special care. Here's everything you need to know to keep your woollen garments looking brand new through winter and beyond.
content:
Wool is a natural fibre, which makes it warm, breathable, and long‑lasting—but it also means it can shrink, stretch, or lose shape if it’s not handled the right way. The golden rule is to treat wool gently. Always check the care label first; if it recommends dry cleaning, avoid machine washing altogether.

If washing at home, use cold water and a mild, wool‑safe detergent. Choose a gentle cycle or, even better, hand‑wash your garments by slowly agitating them in the water instead of scrubbing or twisting. Once washed, never wring wool. Press out the excess water using a clean towel and lay the item flat to dry on a drying rack so it keeps its shape.

Store wool pieces folded rather than hanging to prevent them from stretching at the shoulders. During off‑season months, keep them in breathable storage bags with moth repellents like cedar blocks or lavender sachets. With a bit of extra care, your favourite sweaters, coats, and scarves will stay soft, cosy, and looking new for many winters to come.

title: Dry Cleaning vs Laundry: Which is Better for Your Clothes?
excerpt: Not sure whether to dry clean or wash your garments? We break down exactly when to use each method and why it matters for the life of your clothes.
content:
Many people assume dry cleaning is just a more expensive version of normal washing, but the two processes are actually very different. Traditional laundry uses water and detergent, while dry cleaning relies on specialised cleaning solvents that are gentler on delicate fabrics and structured garments.

You should choose dry cleaning for items like suits, blazers, overcoats, silk dresses, and garments with a “dry clean only” label. The process helps maintain their shape, colour, and finish. Everyday clothing such as t‑shirts, jeans, towels, and most casual wear does perfectly well in a regular wash.

A simple rule of thumb: if the fabric is delicate, heavily structured, or very expensive, let dry cleaning handle it. For sturdy, casual fabrics, regular laundry is usually the best and most economical option. When in doubt, ask your cleaning expert—they can guide you on the safest method so your clothes last longer and look better.

title: 5 Common Stains and How to Remove Them
excerpt: From coffee to ink — we've all had that sinking feeling when something spills. Here are proven techniques to tackle the most common stains before they set.
content:
The key to removing any stain is acting quickly and using the right technique for the type of spill. For coffee and tea stains, start by blotting—never rubbing—to lift as much liquid as possible, then rinse the back of the fabric with cold water and pretreat with a liquid detergent before washing.

For oil and grease stains, sprinkle baking soda or talcum powder on the area to absorb the oil, let it sit for a few minutes, then brush it off and pretreat with a degreasing detergent. Ink stains respond well to alcohol‑based solutions: place a paper towel under the fabric and dab gently with rubbing alcohol until the ink transfers.

Red wine and curry can be tougher, so avoid hot water, which can set the stain. Rinse with cold water, apply a stain remover, and launder as soon as possible. If the garment is delicate or very valuable, it’s always safer to bring it to a professional cleaner so the stain can be treated without damaging the fabric.

title: 7 Benefits of Using a Professional Laundry Service
excerpt: Outsourcing your laundry is not just about saving time. Discover how a professional service can protect your clothes, your schedule, and even your health.
content:
A professional laundry service does far more than simply wash and dry your clothes. Trained staff inspect each garment, sort it correctly, and choose the right detergents and wash cycles for different fabrics. This means less fading, shrinking, and wear compared with home washing.

You also save hours every week that would normally be spent washing, drying, folding, and ironing. For busy families and working professionals, that extra time can go into work, rest, or the things you actually enjoy. Many services also offer pickup and delivery, which turns laundry into a hassle‑free routine.

Another benefit is hygiene. Commercial‑grade machines and processes can remove deep‑seated dirt, allergens, and bacteria more effectively than most domestic washers. Over time, using a professional service helps your clothes last longer, look sharper, and feel fresher—while you enjoy a simpler, more convenient routine.

title: How Often Should You Really Dry Clean Your Clothes?
excerpt: Over‑cleaning can wear out your garments, but under‑cleaning can damage them too. Here’s how to find the right balance for different types of clothing.
content:
There is no single rule for how often you should dry clean everything in your wardrobe—it depends on the fabric, how often you wear it, and in what conditions. Suits worn daily for work usually need cleaning every 3–4 wears, while occasion outfits might only need attention once or twice a season.

Wool coats and jackets can often go through an entire season with just one or two professional cleans, as long as you brush off surface dust and hang them properly between uses. Silk blouses and dresses, on the other hand, pick up body oils and odours more quickly, so cleaning them every 1–3 wears keeps them fresh without over‑treating the fabric.

As a rule, if a garment looks dull, smells musty, or has visible marks, it’s time for a clean. Between visits, hang items on good‑quality hangers, air them out after wearing, and store them in a cool, dry space. This approach keeps your clothes looking polished while avoiding unnecessary wear from over‑cleaning.

title: How to Prepare Your Laundry for Pickup and Delivery
excerpt: Pickup and delivery laundry is super convenient—here’s how to prepare your clothes so they come back perfectly cleaned, pressed, and organised.
content:
Laundry pickup and delivery works best when your clothes are sorted and labelled clearly. Start by separating everyday wash items from delicate or dry‑clean‑only pieces. If your service provides different bags for laundry and dry cleaning, make sure you use them correctly so nothing is processed the wrong way.

Check all pockets for coins, tissues, pens, or receipts—small items can cause big problems in commercial machines. If there are stains you are worried about, mark them with a note or point them out in your booking instructions so the team can pre‑treat them properly.

Finally, close zips, fasten buttons where possible, and tie strings or belts so they don’t get tangled. With a few simple steps before pickup, you help ensure your garments are cleaned efficiently, protected during the process, and returned fresh, neatly folded, and ready to wear.
